evidence_quotes: Tobelo, Indonesia registered 6 events — the highest regional frequency in the digest — including a magnitude 5.7 at 152.9 km depth on 2026-02-14 and a magnitude 5.3 at only 21.4 km depth on 2026-02-04

Three events in the sample dataset were flagged tsunami: true — the magnitude 5.7 at 55 km E of Kermadec Islands (depth 5.7 km, 2026-02-08), the magnitude 5.5 in the New Britain region, PNG (depth 7.4 km, 2026-02-03), and the magnitude 5.5 at 30 km E of Tual, Indonesia (depth 5.4 km, 2026-01-27)

Establish a magnitude threshold alert (suggested: M ≥ 5.5) on real-time monitoring platforms for the Aleutian arc (Nikolski area), Tobelo, and the Kermadec–PNG corridor, and designate a duty officer to review any triggers within the next 24 hours
Brief regional liaisons in Indonesia (North Maluku/Tobelo area) and Chile (Tarapacá region/La Tirana) on the elevated event counts in their jurisdictions — 6 and 4 events respectively
Tobelo, Indonesia warrants priority monitoring given 6 recorded events across a wide depth range (21.4–152.9 km) within the 30-day window
criticisms: The report does not explicitly rank the three tsunami-flagged zones against each other in terms of residual risk priority — a coordinator must infer which of Kermadec, New Britain, or Tual is the highest concern.

Recommended Action 2 asks to 'brief regional liaisons' but does not specify what the briefing should trigger (e.g., pre-position supplies, activate EOC, issue public advisory), leaving the downstream action ambiguous.
The 'usgs-synthetic' caveat is appropriately noted but could be more prominently placed — buried in Data Caveats, a rushed reader might miss it and act on unvalidated data.
